topic.title: The AI didn't take the job, it became the yardstick
topic.claim: AI isn't mainly replacing IT jobs yet, it's being used as a free stick to beat every employee with.
topic.behaviour: Managers compare employee output to what an AI agent could theoretically do, to keep people anxious and compliant.
topic.mechanism: Comparing a person to a machine costs a company nothing and buys silence. Nobody negotiates a raise standing next to something that works for free.
topic.group: IT and services employees, 24-32, watching layoffs and 'AI efficiency' talk around them
topic.moment: You finish a task, and someone casually mentions the AI would've done it in ten minutes. You spend the rest of the day quietly proving you're still worth your seat.

turn.believed: AI is here and it's taking IT jobs.
turn.actually: AI is mostly being used as a benchmark to make everyone feel replaceable, whether or not it could really do the job.

topic.because: A scared employee doesn't ask for a raise or push back on scope. The comparison does the managing so nobody has to.

proof.fact: It is sad to constantly compare a human's work output to an AI agent's... we often tell our senior management to disengage in comparing oranges and apples

topic.payoff: Next time someone brings up what the AI could do, ask what it actually did yesterday.
topic.send_to: Anyone in IT dreading their next 1:1.
real_details: TCS cut nearly 20,000 roles in a recent quarter
WEF estimates 88% of India's IT services work is AI-exposed
An employee got a performance warning in their third month on a new job
After the warning, they focused on understanding the role and raised their rating to B+/A
A new, more experienced teammate worked slower and leaned heavily on AI, getting the same warning
That teammate got emotional once or twice saying they were trying their best
topic.news_peg: ThePrint ground report on AI reshaping IT's billable-hours model, published 2026-10-19
topic.why_now: Lands the same week as appraisal-season anxiety, compounding the mood

score.why: The AI-comparison dig at work is instantly recognisable, and the reframe, it's a management tool not a threat, is the one-step-further the page wants.

sources.fact: ThePrint's ground report finds mixed evidence. Xpheno's Kamal Karanth says AI has not yet visibly caused significant layoffs, which partly supports the claim. A Cognizant HR associate calls the constant comparison of human output to an AI agent's "sad", but the article does not report managers using that comparison as a pressure tactic.
sources.excerpt: "AI hasn't really shown up as a visible cause of significant layoffs or restructured hiring funnel through 2026." (Kamal Karanth, Xpheno) | "Suddenly, 2021 onwards, we started over-hiring" (Phani Pattamatta, HYSEA) | "It is sad to constantly compare a human's work output to an AI agent's." (Cognizant HR associate) | "At 1.23 lakh, active tech jobs in India in October marked an 18-month high."

sources.fact: Five big Indian IT firms posted a net headcount decline of 7,389 in FY26, the first in two decades. Forkast links this to AI, but TCS's CEO attributes TCS's cuts to skill mismatches rather than AI productivity gains.
sources.excerpt: "posted the first net headcount decline in two decades in FY26, shedding 7,389 employees." | TCS CEO K. Krithivasan: "This is not because of AI giving some 20 per cent productivity gains." | TeamLease executive: "companies are hiring fewer people as a matter of caution."

cover.headline: AI hasn't taken your IT job. It's taken your [hike conversation].
cover.sub: Comparing you to a machine costs nothing. It buys your silence.

paragraphs: AI hasn't taken your IT job. It's taken your hike conversation.
slides.why_swipe: How does a tool that hasn't replaced me still cost me my raise?

paragraphs: You finally close the ticket that ate your week: three days of logs, two late client calls, one fix that holds.
In standup your lead says it lightly. "AI would've done this in ten minutes, na." Everyone laughs. You laugh too, a second late.
slides.why_swipe: What does that one line do to the weeks after it?

paragraphs: For the next few weeks you reply to every Teams message within a minute, and your green dot stays on till nine.
In the 1:1 before appraisals, a new module lands on your plate. You type "sure, will do" before reading it. The hike you rehearsed in the shower never comes up.
slides.why_swipe: So is AI actually coming for your seat, or not?

paragraphs: Yes, the tools are real, and you probably have one open in another tab right now, fixing your regex. But Xpheno's Kamal Karanth says AI hasn't shown up as a visible cause of significant layoffs through 2026.
**The comparison is cheaper than the tool. Once you're scared, it does the managing.**
slides.why_swipe: Then what happens the next time someone says ten minutes?

paragraphs: The ten-minute line comes back the week before appraisals, same lead, same light tone, same laugh waiting to happen. This time someone asks, "Okay. What did it actually do yesterday?"
**The room goes silent. Then your lead says, "Let's take this offline."**

end.save: Read it again the night before your next 1:1.
end.send: Anyone in IT who laughed a second late in standup this week.

draft.alt_text: A five-slide carousel. Cover headline: AI hasn't taken your IT job. It's taken your hike conversation. The slides follow a typical IT employee who fixes a hard ticket and hears in standup that AI would have done it in ten minutes. Over the following weeks they reply to messages within a minute, stay online till nine, accept a new module without reading it and never bring up their hike in the appraisal 1:1. The post admits AI tools are real, notes that Xpheno's Kamal Karanth says AI hasn't visibly caused significant layoffs through 2026, and argues the comparison is cheaper than the tool and keeps staff quiet. It ends with someone asking what the AI actually did yesterday, the room going silent, and the lead saying let's take this offline.

claims.text: Xpheno's Kamal Karanth says AI hasn't shown up as a visible cause of significant layoffs through 2026.
